business.description: Maral Overseas Limited is an integrated textile company with capabilities across yarns, fabrics and garments. Its yarn and fabric manufacturing operations are centred at the Maral Sarovar facility in Khargone, Madhya Pradesh, while garmenting operations are based in the NCR region.

outlook.statement: Scale presence in EU and other FTA-enabled markets with focus and urgency; expand value-added portfolio building on success of melange and dyed yarn; sustain cost discipline, deepen operational efficiencies and convert improving productivity gains into stronger profitability as conditions improve

India–EU FTA expected to be operational with ratification in 2026; Indian textile exports to EU could grow from ~US$7 billion to US$30 billion over medium term; Bangladesh graduation from LDC status in late 2026 to erode its duty-free access in EU over time

Proposed captive solar power plant (15 MW) expected to support portion of energy requirements through renewable energy, reduce dependence on conventional energy sources, lower carbon footprint, improve long-term energy cost efficiency and strengthen alignment with evolving ESG and regulatory expectations; CO2 emission reduction of 17,220 tonnes p.a. (37,622 tonnes in FY2027 with zero coal)

Demand is expected to strengthen further, driven by a gradual recovery in key apparel markets such as the United States and European Union, alongside the continued momentum of the China+1 sourcing strategy. Finalisation of the India–EU Free Trade Agreement and the rollover of the India–UK Free Trade Agreement are expected to enhance export competitiveness further.

In FY2027, the Indian economy is poised to achieve accelerated growth relative to the preceding year, with real GDP forecast to expand by 7% to 7.4%, buoyed by resilient private consumption. Strategic trade agreements with pivotal partners, including the United Kingdom, the United States, and the European Union, are anticipated to deepen bilateral commerce by enhancing market access for goods and services.

The global textile market is expected to grow to US$1,955.50 billion by 2034, with a CAGR of 7.11%. The industry is poised for sustained expansion, driven by innovation, digital integration, and a continued shift towards sustainable and resilient supply chains.
Demand is expected to strengthen further in FY2027, driven by recovery in key apparel markets such as the US and EU, along with the ongoing China+1 sourcing shift.

The finalisation of the India–EU Free Trade Agreement (FTA), along with the rollover of the India–UK FTA, is expected to provide a further boost, opening new avenues for growth and strengthening India's position in the global apparel market.
The continued emphasis on value-added products and prudent business decisions is expected to support performance in the coming years.

The sector's strong raw material base, skilled workforce, and growing domestic demand provide resilience. Maral has effectively navigated recent challenges and strengthened its operational resilience, positioning itself to capitalise on emerging opportunities across global value chains, supported by policy thrust, modern manufacturing investments, and deeper integration into export markets.

Focus on innovation, value addition, and sustainability; multiple developments progressed to bulk order stage; strong approval ratio across key global brands and domestic suppliers; sustainability adding significant value to portfolio (cotton/linen blends, recycled polyester developments).

Plan to install steam traps and condensate recovery system, regular monitoring of air/steam/water leakages, energy-efficient timer lighting, VFD on supply/return fans in preparatory humidification plant (Units 4 & 5), improve boiler steam ratio, reduce ETP treatment and chemical costs, install 20,000 Eco HLLD spindles with unique bolster design for energy saving, reduce frame size in four melange sampling ring frames (replace 30 kW motors with 11 kW, saving ~1.8 lakh units annually), recover condensates and reuse waste as boiler feed water.

Upon notification of the related Rules to the New Labour Codes by the Central/State Government and any further clarification on other aspects of the New Labour Codes, the Company will evaluate and account for additional impact, if any, in subsequent periods.

The Company has been tightening operations, scaling value-added capacity and steadily restoring profitability, is well placed to participate in this next chapter from a position of strength. Further, these efforts coupled with gradual improvement in business operations would result in a sequential recovery in financial performance. Also, the continued emphasis on value-added products and prudent business decisions is expected to support performance in the coming years.

Salary risk: Actual salary increase will increase the Plan's liability. Increase in assumption of salary increase rate in future valuations will also increase the liability.
Investment risk: If Plan is funded, then assets liabilities mismatch & actual return on investment assets is lower than the discount rate assumed at the last valuation date, can impact the liability.
Discount rate risk: Reduction in discount rate in subsequent valuations can increase the plan's liability.
Mortality & disability risk: Actual deaths & disability cases proving lower or higher than assumed in the valuation can impact the liabilities.
Withdrawals: Actual withdrawals proving higher or lower than assumed withdrawals and change of withdrawal rates at subsequent valuations can impact Plan's liability.
